findings.title: Sensitive operation answers anonymous callers
findings.description: Requests with no credential at all got a 2xx response from an endpoint that returns sensitive data or changes state.

findings.recommendation: Add authentication to POST /consumers in ftgo-api-gateway.
mitigation: Require a verified token on this operation in the service itself, not only at the gateway.
Reject requests without Authorization with 401 before any business logic runs.
Add a test that calls the endpoint anonymously and expects 401.

findings.title: Secret stored in plaintext in the deployment manifest
findings.description: An environment variable with a secret-looking name has its value written directly in the manifest, so anyone with read access to the repo or cluster config has it.
findings.detail: SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD is written in plaintext in the ftgo-consumer-service manifest
evidence: env SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD: source=plaintext (value not copied by the extractor)
findings.recommendation: Move SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD of ftgo-consumer-service into a Secret and rotate it.
mitigation: Move the value into a Kubernetes Secret (or a vault) and reference it with secretKeyRef.
Rotate the exposed value: it is already in version control history.
Add a CI check that fails on plaintext env values with secret-like names.
findings.snippet:
env:
  - name: JWT_SECRET
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef: {name: shoplite-secrets, key: jwt-secret}

findings.title: No network segmentation for the service
findings.description: No NetworkPolicy selects this workload, so every pod in the cluster can call it. One compromised pod can move laterally.
findings.detail: ftgo-dynamodb-local-init accepts traffic from any pod
evidence: callers seen in traces: none (only external clients)
findings.recommendation: Add a NetworkPolicy for ftgo-dynamodb-local-init allowing only: the ingress controller.
mitigation: Add a default-deny NetworkPolicy for the namespace, then allow only the callers seen in traces.
